newsitem.title: INDIA: India courts directs cellular operators to TRAI.
newsitem.headline: India courts directs cellular operators to TRAI.

text.p: An Indian court on Monday dismissed all pending cases by cellular telephone operators challenging a government order over a recent tariff hike, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency said the court directed them to appeal to an independent regulatory body the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI).

The cellular operators had asked the Delhi High Court to overturn an order of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) which they said set prohibitively high tariff rates for calls from basic, fixed-line phones to mobile units.
The DoT in a January 29 order set tariff rates which the operators said were far higher than warranted except in the four metro cities of Bombay, Calcutta, Delhi and Madras.
The order did not seek to alter the normal fixed-line charges in the four cities.

The operators contended that under the rates set by the order, a phone call from a basic phone to a cellular unit within the same area, or circle, would cost the user of the basic phone about 10 rupees a minute compared with the current 1.40 rupees.
Cellular operators, admitted under an economic liberalisation programme, launched their services in 1995, starting with the four metro cities.

The court, before disposing of the matter, refused to grant any stay on the hike, which became effective from February 15 in all states except the four metro areas, and said the petitioner could ask for the interim stay on the hike from the TRAI.
